annotationRationale: The derivation interprets circle equations, computes coordinate-region and circle areas, and uses their ratio for uniform probability. A perfect-square identity proves the needed containment.
sourceMethod: Followed the official square and annulus area calculation. Added an algebraic proof of the containment that the official solution describes through tangency.

review.mathCheck: The target is the closed annulus 18≤x²+y²≤32, of area 14π. The inequality (|x|+|y|)²≤2(x²+y²)≤64 proves containment in the square, with tangencies at (±4,±4). The board has area 128, giving probability 7π/64 and m+n=71, choice B. Boundary inclusion does not affect area.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 14, pages 6–7: identify the square and annulus, then divide their areas. The algebraic containment proof justifies the official tangency observation. The candidate correctly places the upper vertex at (0,8), correcting the source diagram's duplicated (8,0) label.
review.annotationCheck: Geometric probability and circle interpretation are appropriate assessed nodes. Coordinate area, circle area and perfect-square expansion are all used as support; no incorrect direct node or material omission.
